spec: Part VIII 8.1 — removing a set inside a live session (V54–V55); Appendix A A11 (owner-directed 2026-09-09). Before this the SessionModel action surface had addSet and addWarmup and no way back: one accidental tap changed the workout's denominator forever, and that denominator feeds the live x/y line, the celebration, the shared post summary and the journal.

vectors.title: removing a set renumbers the remainder and recomputes the denominator
vectors.spec: 8.1 V54; A11 (order stays dense so a later patch cannot address a hole); Flow 3 (warm-ups are excluded from every count)
vectors.rule: removeSet(sets, order) drops the row at that order and renumbers every survivor from zero, preserving their relative order. setsPlanned counts work sets only — a removed warm-up never changes x/y, and a removed work set always does.
vectors.reviewNote: Renumbering is what makes removal safe on the wire: SetLogDTO carries no id, so a set's POSITION is its identity across the sync boundary (logged in debt.md). A sparse order after a removal would let a concurrent patch write to the wrong row.

vectors.title: an exercise never drops below one work set
vectors.spec: 8.1 V55; A11; Flow 3 (a set row IS the exercise — one with no rows can be neither logged nor skipped)
vectors.rule: Removing the last remaining WORK set is refused: the sets come back unchanged and removed is false. The floor counts work sets only, so it still refuses when warm-ups are present — a warm-up is excluded from x/y, completion and personal records, and an exercise made of warm-ups alone would report 0/0.
vectors.reviewNote: The refusal is silent at the engine level; the UI is what tells the user (the control is simply absent on a single-set exercise). The server carries the same guard, so an offline phone cannot push a session past it either.
